narratives.strongestCase: Outside India the causal record mostly finds incumbents rewarded: PANES in Uruguay (Manacorda et al 2011), Progresa (De La O 2013), Bolsa Família (Zucco 2013; Hunter & Power 2007), 4Ps in the Philippines (Labonne 2013). narratives.strongestCounter: Imai, King & Velasco Rivera (2020) re-analysed Progresa and found no partisan effect; Zucco finds Bolsa effects that do not build lasting loyalty; Deshpande et al find MGNREGA and pension recipients less likely to vote BJP, so ‘transfers → incumbent’ is scheme-specific; the Lokniti Maharashtra team itself says a 3-point gender gap is not proof; no Indian scheme has a causal vote estimate (0 of 8 here). ‘Buy’ also implies an exchange the Supreme Court (Balaji 2013) says is lawful policy, not corrupt practice.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A quasi-experimental estimate for an Indian scheme (eligibility discontinuity or staggered rollout) showing a vote effect, or a null one; Lokniti cross-tabs by beneficiary status.

symmetryCheck: Same lens on every party. BJP: MP Ladli Behna (launched months before Nov 2023; 80% coverage; won), Maharashtra Ladki Bahin (first payment 2024-08-14, election three months later; ₹2,100 promised, ₹1,500 paid, ₹500 for overlap after the win), Delhi and Haryana schemes announced after the PM's 2022 anti-freebie speech. INC: Kamal Nath's matching ₹1,500 promise in MP; Karnataka's Gruha Lakshmi flips the state from revenue surplus to deficit (PRS); Telangana and Himachal counted among the 12 UCT states. INC/UPA-era MGNREGA and NFSA are the schemes the Aadhaar-exclusion literature (Khera, Drèze) and the Bihar RCTs test — leakage in Congress-era programmes is as documented as exclusion in BJP-era authentication. TMC (Lakshmir Bhandar) and Assam (Orunodoi) both raised allocations after their elections (PRS: +15%, +31%), which cuts against ‘cut once won’ for both a BJP and a non-BJP state. DMK/AIADMK: the 2013 Supreme Court freebies case arose from both parties' manifestos. JMM raised Maiya Samman before Jharkhand's 2024 poll. AAP (Delhi ₹1,000 promise, Dec 2024) lost; the BJP (₹2,500, Mar 2025) then enacted a larger one. What the file cannot do symmetrically: no survey evidence for Karnataka 2023 or West Bengal 2021, no primary record on the Bengal MGNREGA stoppage, and no causal vote estimate for any party's scheme — the voids are recorded rather than filled.
